issues.description: The solution makes Genre.name private (private let name: String) but the Client implementation reads genre.name to print the genre name. This is an internal visibility conflict: with name declared private in Bookstore.swift, code in Client.swift (a different file) cannot access it, which would cause a compilation error and prevent students from following the example output requirements. The problem statement requires that Genre exposes a name (used for printing), but the solution's private modifier blocks that usage.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Genre name accessible to other files in the module. Remove the private modifier (use the default internal visibility) or declare it as public/fileprivate as appropriate. For example, change 'private let name: String' to 'let name: String' (or 'public let name: String') so the Client can read and print the genre name.
